messages.subject: Major update to tidyLPA available
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

First, if you have posted a question to the mailing list over the past few months and have not yet received a response, I apologize – please look for one soon. One reason for the delay is that we have been working on a major revision to tidyLPA. That major revision resulted in a new version—version 1.0.0—which is now available on GitHub.

You can read about the new version here: https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/index.html

You can also read more about the changes and the rationale for making them here:  https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/articles/introduction-to-major-changes.html

We would welcome any feedback on the new version before we submit it to CRAN. It can be installed using the devtools package, i.e.:

install.packages <https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/utils/topics/install.packages>("devtools")
devtools::install_github <https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/devtools/topics/reexports>("data-edu/tidyLPA")

Thank you for your interest in the tidyLPA package. Please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions—about the update or anything else—and we’ll try to respond more quickly than we have.

Josh

--

Joshua M. Rosenberg, Ph.D. <http://joshuamrosenberg.com/>

Assistant Professor, STEM Education

Dept. of Theory and Practice in Teacher Education

The University of Tennessee, Knoxville

420 Claxton, 1122 Volunteer Boulevard, Knoxville, TN 37996

(865) 974-5973

jmros...@utk.edu

messages.subject: Re: Question about the entropy statistic
messages.body_plain:
Hi, thank you for your question - and I'm sorry for the delay. We have made a change to how entropy is calculated in the most recent version. If you are still curious about this, consider installing the (most recent) development version via the following commands:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("data-edu/tidyLPA")

There are a few differences to the interface to be aware of, too (can check the README here: https://data-edu.github.io/tidyLPA/).

Thank you for your patience with this.
Josh
:

>
> I had a quick question on the entropy fit statistic. I fit a 2, 3, and 4 profile LPA to a data set with 65,000 individuals. There are 7 indicators that the individuals are measured on. > Best,

messages.subject: Re: Adding covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi, and thank you for your question. We do not provide functionality to include covariates - we recommend that these be carried out using MPlus. Our reasoning is that we want to keep the scope of tidyLPA narrow - and to only include functionality that can be carried out with both MPlus and mclust.

Thank you for understanding!
Josh

messages.subject: Re: Models could not be estimated error
messages.subject_clean: Models could not be estimated error
messages.body_plain:
Patrick, thank you for your message. I'm sorry for the delay. It is somewhat hard (for me) to say why the model may not converge, so I'll try not to speculate, but I think it basically suggests that the specification of the model isn't adequate for the parameters to be estimated.

I understand what you mean regarding constraining the variances to be equal when your substantive knowledge indicates they shouldn't be. I would consider estimating that constrained model just to try to understand what is going on better: if it converges, it may well suggest that the model with varying variances is too complex (perhaps for this particular sample).

Sorry it's hard to say more. I'm sorry for the delay, too. Do let us know if you have further questions - we'll try to answer more promptly going forward.
-Josh

> Hi all,
>
> I thought I would add some more information in case this helps you respond to my original question, which I know was rather vague!  But I played around some more and it seems like the issue is being largely caused by some specific subscales, the Low Energy/Weak subscale and also (to some extent) the Movement Sensitivity subscale.  When these subscales are not included, I am able to estimate a few profiles with varying variances.
>
> The dataset I'm working with includes both autistic and neurotypical participants, and this the LEW and MS subscales have a somewhat peculiar pattern.  Most of the neurotypical participants have scores that are practically at ceiling, with rare exceptions, while there is a lot more variability among the autistic participants.
>
> Does anyone have thoughts about how to resolve this situation?  Theoretically speaking, constraining the profiles to have equal variances when we know that two important populations have distinctly unequal variances seems quite problematic, but I also don't want to toss out these subscales and lose all the information in them!
>
> Thanks so much.

messages.subject: Re: tidyLPA and profile number for each case
messages.subject_clean: tidyLPA and profile number for each case
messages.body_plain:
Dear Soile, thank you so much for your message - and I'm sorry for the delay! This is a good question. It should be output by the estimate_profiles() function. If you save that output to an object, i.e., my_output (e.g., my_output <- estimate_profiles(d, V1, V2, V3, n_profiles = 3)), you should be able to use my_output as a data frame with the observations and the cases.

Note that the development version of tidyLPA includes a helper function, get_data(), which will return this, i.e. get_data(my_output).

Do be in touch with any questions - we'll try to respond much more promptly next time.

Best,
Josh

messages.subject: Re: New to tidyLPA, mclust, and Mplus: a few questions from a newbie
messages.subject_clean: New to tidyLPA, mclust, and Mplus: a few questions from a newbie
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dalin, thank you for your questions. I'm sorry for the delay. Please see my responses in-line below:

>
> 1. Is mclust effectively integrated into tidyLPA? Would there be any advantage to utilizing both mclust and tidyLPA separately?

It is - especially in the new version, in which we add some functionality (in terms of measures of fit, plotting, and model selection, in particular). There may be some cases in which you may wish to use mclust, of course - it is a very feature-full package.

> 2. I'm not sure if this is the correct phrasing, but it appears that tidyLPA can be implemented with Mplus using MplusAutomation. Is this a fair statement?

Yes, that's right! Using Mplus (and MplusAutomation) requires that you have purchased and installed Mplus - that's the only 'catch'.

>
> 3. What is the advantage of using tidyLPA and Mplus? Most of the papers I've read conducting LPA have used Mplus. As I learn R, I'm concerned about becoming overwhelmed by also having to learn Mplus. I guess that is at the core of my question regarding using both.

In short, providing an interface through R to Mplus has benefits: some of the tedious parts are obviated (i.e., preparing the data in Mplus format; working with the .out files generated by Mplus), and it is easier to run and compare output from a variety of model specifications. Additionally, writing Mplus syntax can be a challenge, especially for very complex models. tidyLPA makes this easier.

> 4. I am submitting a grant and am wondering if it is worth budgeting in Mplus, which will probably be contingent to responses to the above questions.

In the development version of tidyLPA, we have worked very hard to make it so that there is comparable functionality between Mplus and mclust. I would say that the primary reason to use Mplus is to carry out more complex analyses, i.e., to include covariate or distal outcomes, or to account for more complex data structures.

> 5. Relatedly, this is a a project I'm working on with another institution who does not have Mplus but has R. Would utilizing Mplus preclude easily sharing files with this other site, or can tidyLPA in R still be used to easily share data (which goes back to question 3)?
>

Yes, utilizing Mplus would likely preclude sharing files with the other site - unless they had access to Mplus. Mplus is proprietary and commercial; I don't think there's really any way around these facts!

Hope this helps! Thanks Dalin for your questions.
-Josh
